paragraphs.title: Samuel Establishes His Integrity and the Change of Leadership

easy.explanation: Samuel says that he listened to the people and made a king over them.
easy.q: Whom did Samuel make king over Israel?

easy.explanation: Samuel says, “I am old and grayheaded.”
easy.q: What does Samuel say about his age?

easy.explanation: Samuel asks the people to witness against him before the Lord and His anointed.
easy.q: Before whom does Samuel ask the people to witness against him?

answers: To prove that he had not abused his leadership
To ask them to make him king
To choose his sons as rulers
medium.explanation: He asks whether he had taken property, oppressed anyone, or accepted a bribe.
medium.q: Why does Samuel ask the people to witness against him?

medium.explanation: Samuel presents himself openly so the people can testify about his conduct.
medium.q: What does Samuel mean when he says, “Behold, here I am”?

answers: That he had taken everything from them
That he had not defrauded or oppressed them
medium.explanation: The people say Samuel had not defrauded, oppressed, or taken anything from them.
medium.q: What do the people testify concerning Samuel?

answers: He says his sons became kings
He contrasts his former leadership with the king now ruling before them
He says his sons led Israel out of Egypt
challenge.explanation: Samuel mentions his age and sons while pointing to the king who now walks before Israel.
challenge.q: How does Samuel connect his age and his sons with the change of leadership?

challenge.explanation: Samuel invites public examination of his leadership and financial conduct.
challenge.q: What quality of Samuel is emphasized by his public questioning?

answers: The Lord, His anointed, and the people
challenge.explanation: Samuel cites the Lord and His anointed as witnesses, and the people affirm the testimony.
challenge.q: Who confirms that nothing was found in Samuel’s hand?

paragraphs.title: Reviewing God’s Goodness and Israel’s Deliverance

easy.explanation: Samuel says that the Lord sent Moses and Aaron and brought their fathers out of Egypt.
easy.q: Who brought Israel’s fathers up out of Egypt?

answers: They were delivered into the hands of enemies
easy.explanation: The Lord sold them into the hands of Sisera, the Philistines, and the king of Moab.
easy.q: What happened when Israel forgot the Lord their God?

answers: Sisera and the king of Moab
easy.explanation: Moses and Aaron brought the fathers of Israel out of Egypt.
easy.q: Who brought Israel’s fathers out of Egypt?

answers: Forgetting the Lord, oppression, crying out, and deliverance
Deliverance, oppression, leaving Egypt, and crying out
medium.explanation: The people forgot the Lord, suffered under enemies, cried out, and were delivered.
medium.q: What main sequence of events is described?

answers: They called to Him for help
medium.explanation: The people appealed to the Lord for deliverance from their enemies.
medium.q: What does “they cried unto the Lord” mean in this passage?

answers: The people cried unto the Lord and confessed their sin
They chose the king of Moab
medium.explanation: The people confessed that they had sinned and asked the Lord to deliver them.
medium.q: What led to deliverance after the oppression?

answers: Deliverance came through leaders sent by the Lord
challenge.explanation: The Lord sent Jerubbaal, Bedan, Jephthah, and Samuel to deliver Israel.
challenge.q: What does the list of deliverers show?

answers: Forgetting the Lord is presented before Israel is delivered to its enemies
There is no relationship between them
Forgetting the Lord led Israel out of Egypt
challenge.explanation: The passage places Israel’s forgetting of the Lord before its oppression by enemies.
challenge.q: What relationship is shown between forgetting the Lord and oppression?

answers: The Lord’s righteous acts and deliverance
Only the strength of its enemies
challenge.explanation: Samuel calls attention to the Lord’s acts in bringing out and delivering His people.
challenge.q: What does Samuel want Israel to remember in this historical review?

paragraphs.title: The Request for a King and the Conditions of Faithfulness

easy.explanation: Samuel says that the Lord their God was their king.
easy.q: Who was Israel’s king according to Samuel?

answers: A king to reign over them
easy.explanation: The people said, “Nay; but a king shall reign over us.”
easy.q: What did the people request when Nahash came against them?

easy.explanation: The Lord set a king over them—the king they had chosen and desired.
easy.q: What did the Lord set over Israel?

answers: If they feared, served, and obeyed the Lord
If they stopped serving the Lord
medium.explanation: Samuel requires fear of the Lord, service, obedience, and refusal to rebel.
medium.q: On what condition would both the people and the king continue following the Lord?

answers: To refuse to speak to the people
To refuse to choose a king
medium.explanation: To rebel means to resist or disobey the Lord’s commandment.
medium.q: What does “rebel against the commandment of the Lord” mean?

answers: The hand of the Lord would be against them
They would live securely without warning
medium.explanation: Samuel warns that the Lord’s hand would be against them as it was against their fathers.
medium.q: What would happen if the people would not obey the Lord?

answers: Both the king and the people remain subject to the Lord
The king is exempt from obedience
challenge.explanation: The king must follow the Lord just as the people must.
challenge.q: What is the relationship between the human king and the Lord?

answers: His threat prompted Israel to ask for a king
He was the king of Israel
He led Israel out of Egypt
challenge.explanation: When Israel saw Nahash coming against them, they demanded a human king.
challenge.q: Why is Nahash king of Ammon mentioned?

answers: The king was given in response to the people’s request
The people did not want a king
challenge.explanation: Samuel reminds them that they chose and desired a king, and the Lord set him over them.
challenge.q: What does “the king whom ye have chosen” emphasize?

paragraphs.title: The Heavenly Sign and the People’s Confession

easy.explanation: Samuel said the Lord would send thunder and rain.
easy.q: What sign did Samuel say the Lord would send?

answers: During the building of the tabernacle
easy.explanation: Samuel asked whether it was not wheat harvest that day.
easy.q: When did Samuel say the sign would occur?

answers: They greatly feared the Lord and Samuel
easy.explanation: The people greatly feared the Lord and Samuel when thunder and rain came.
easy.q: How did the people react to the sign?

answers: It occurred during wheat harvest and confirmed Samuel’s warning
medium.explanation: The unusual thunder and rain confirmed Samuel’s words about their sinful request for a king.
medium.q: Why did the sign show the greatness of the people’s wickedness?

answers: The time when wheat is gathered
medium.explanation: Harvest is the gathering of a crop, here specifically wheat.

answers: Pray for them unto the Lord
medium.explanation: They asked Samuel to pray for them so that they would not die.
medium.q: What did the people ask Samuel to do after the sign?

answers: The sign showed that asking for a king had been wicked in the Lord’s sight
The sign proved that the people had not sinned
challenge.explanation: Samuel says the thunder and rain revealed the wickedness of asking for a king.
challenge.q: What connection does Samuel make between the sign and the request for a king?

answers: They recognized their sin and Samuel’s role as an intercessor
challenge.explanation: The people confessed that they had added this evil to their sins and asked Samuel to pray.
challenge.q: What does the people’s request for prayer reveal?

challenge.explanation: The verse says that all the people greatly feared the Lord and Samuel.
challenge.q: Whom did the people greatly fear after the thunder and rain?

paragraphs.title: Encouragement, Prayer, and the Upright Path

easy.explanation: Samuel tells them not to turn aside from following the Lord.
easy.q: From whom did Samuel tell the people not to turn aside?

answers: Praying for the people and teaching them
easy.explanation: Samuel says he will not cease to pray for them and will teach them the good and right way.
easy.q: What did Samuel promise to continue doing?

easy.explanation: The Lord would not forsake His people for His great name’s sake.
easy.q: What did Samuel say the Lord would not do?

answers: Vain things cannot profit or deliver
Vain things are another way to serve the Lord
medium.explanation: Samuel says that vain things cannot profit or deliver because they are vain.
medium.q: Why did Samuel warn the people not to turn aside after vain things?

answers: Strong rejection of committing the sin he describes
medium.explanation: Samuel strongly rejects the idea of ceasing to pray for the people.
medium.q: What does “God forbid” express in Samuel’s statement?

answers: Fearing the Lord, serving Him truly, and obeying Him
medium.explanation: Samuel teaches the people to fear and serve the Lord with all their heart.
medium.q: What is the good and right way Samuel will teach?

answers: He tells the people not to fear while warning them not to turn from the Lord
challenge.explanation: Samuel reassures them with “Fear not” but still commands them to follow and serve the Lord.
challenge.q: How does Samuel combine encouragement with warning?

answers: He regards prayer and instruction as duties toward the people
He asks to be released from all responsibility
He transfers his responsibility to the enemies
challenge.explanation: Samuel considers it sinful to cease praying and commits himself to teaching the people.
challenge.q: How are Samuel’s prayer and teaching connected to his responsibility as leader?

answers: They and their king will be consumed
challenge.explanation: Samuel concludes that if they continue to do wickedly, both they and their king will be consumed.
challenge.q: What warning is given if the people continue to do wickedly?
